voices.note: ואמרי לה כדי (2b.18) -- the tradition that the dictum was said without attribution
דתניא (2b.13), reporting R' Yehoshua ben Korcha
the ואיתימא chain naming R' Chiyya bar Abba (2b.22, 2b.23, 3a.4, 3a.11)
the heavenly voice in R' Yirmeya's narrative (3a.4, 3a.6)
ואמרי לה (3a.8) -- the variant of Rav's derasha: אלו המסורות
anonymous redactorial voice: the ואימא challenges, מנלן, מאי טעמא, בשלמא, עד כמה, ותסברא, מאי שנא, מאן נינהו, מאי תקנתיה

props.gloss_en: the mishna: the walled cities that read on the fifteenth are those walled since the days of Joshua son of Nun
Rava: since the unwalled read on the fourteenth (Esther 9:19), the walled read on the fifteenth
since it is written 'the fourteenth day and ET the fifteenth day', the ET interrupts: these on the fourteenth and those on the fifteenth
'in their times' (Esther 9:31): the time of this one is not the time of that one
[the walled cities read] like Shushan
remembering [the reading] is on the days of observing: 'and these days are remembered and observed' (Esther 9:28) likens remembering to observing
R' Yehoshua ben Korcha: cities walled since the days of Ahasuerus read on the fifteenth
the gezera shava prazi / prazi (Esther 9:19 -- Deut 3:5) is valid
Shushan is different, since the miracle was done in it
for our tanna: 'every province and province' distinguishes walled since Joshua from walled since Ahasuerus
for our tanna: 'every city and city' distinguishes Shushan from other cities
for RYBK: 'every province and province' distinguishes Shushan from other cities
rather, the verse comes for a derasha -- that of R' Yehoshua ben Levi
R' Yehoshua ben Levi: a walled city, and all that is adjacent to it and all that is seen with it, is judged as a walled city
how far [is 'adjacent']? as from Chamtan to Tiberias -- a mil
the measure of a mil is as from Chamtan to Tiberias
R' Yirmeya (or R' Chiyya bar Abba): mem, nun, tzadi, peh, kaf [final forms] -- the Seers said them
'these are the commandments' (Lev 27:34) -- a prophet may not innovate anything from now on
Rav Chisda: the mem and samekh in the tablets stood by a miracle
yes, they existed, but it was not known which belongs in the middle of a word and which at the end; the Seers came and established open forms medially and closed forms finally
rather, they forgot them, and [the Seers] re-established them
the Targum of the Torah -- Onkelos the convert said it from the mouth of R' Eliezer and R' Yehoshua
the Targum of the Prophets -- Yonatan ben Uzziel said it from the mouth of Chaggai, Zechariah and Malachi
and the Land of Israel quaked, four hundred parasangs by four hundred parasangs [at the Targum of the Prophets]
a bat kol: who is this who has revealed My secrets to mankind?
Yonatan ben Uzziel: I revealed Your secrets -- not for my honour nor my father's house, but for Yours, so that disputes not multiply in Israel
and he sought further to reveal a Targum of the Writings
a bat kol said to him: enough for you
why? because it [the Writings] contains the end of the Messiah
Rav: 'and they read in the book, the Torah of God' (Neh 8:8) -- this is the scriptural text
Rav: 'distinctly' -- this is the Targum
Rav: 'and they gave the sense' -- these are the verse divisions
Rav: 'and they caused them to understand the reading' -- these are the cantillation divisions
and some say: these are the masorot
they [the Targum of the Torah] forgot it, and [Onkelos] re-established it
of the Torah -- the matter is explicit [so its Targum revealed nothing hidden]
of the Prophets -- some matters are explicit and some are obscure
as it is written: 'on that day the mourning in Jerusalem shall be great, like the mourning of Hadadrimmon in the valley of Megiddon' (Zech 12:11) -- an obscure matter
Rav Yosef: were it not for the Targum of this verse, I would not know what it says

the Targum Rav Yosef quotes: like the mourning for Ahab son of Omri, whom Hadadrimmon son of Tavrimmon slew in Ramot Gilead, and for Josiah son of Amon, whom Pharaoh the lame slew in the valley of Megiddo
who are 'the men who were with me' (Dan 10:7)? Chaggai, Zechariah and Malachi
they were greater than he, for they were prophets and he was not a prophet
he was greater than they, for he saw and they did not see
since they did not see, why were they frightened? though they did not see, their mazal saw
Ravina: learn from this -- one who is frightened, though he himself sees nothing, his mazal sees
what is his remedy? let him recite the Shema
and if he stands in a filthy place, let him move four cubits from his place
and if not, let him say thus: 'the goat of the slaughterhouse is fatter than I'

schemas.gloss_en: אשכחן עשייה, זכירה מנלן? 'נזכרים ונעשים' -- remembering is likened to observing, so the reading is on the same days
מאי טעמא דרבי יהושע בן קרחה? כי שושן: as Shushan, walled since Ahasuerus, reads on the fifteenth, so every city walled since Ahasuerus reads on the fifteenth
ותנא דידן מאי טעמא? יליף פרזי פרזי: 'הפרזים' (Esther 9:19) / 'ערי הפרזי' (Deut 3:5) -- as there walled since Joshua, so here

supports.gloss_en: וכדרבי יהושע בן לוי הוא דאתא -- the doubled words of Esther 9:28 ground the adjacent-and-visible rule
דכתיב: ביום ההוא יגדל המספד ... כמספד הדדרמון בבקעת מגדון (Zech 12:11)
ואמר רב יוסף: אלמלא תרגומא דהאי קרא לא ידענא מאי קאמר
שמע מינה -- from Daniel's companions, frightened because their mazal saw

objections.gloss_en: ואימא: פרזים בארבעה עשר, מוקפין כלל כלל לא! -- say the walled do not celebrate at all

answered_by.gloss_en: ולאו ישראל נינהו? ועוד: מהודו ועד כוש כתיב (Esther 1:1) -- are they not Jews? and the kingdom ran from Hodu to Cush

objections.gloss_en: ואימא: פרזים בארביסר, מוקפין בארביסר ובחמיסר, כדכתיב: להיות עושים את יום ארבעה עשר ואת יום חמשה עשר (Esther 9:21)

answered_by.gloss_en: had it said 'the fourteenth and fifteenth', as you say; now that it says 'ואת יום', the ET interrupts (= p_et_mafsik)

objections.gloss_en: ואימא: פרזים בארביסר, מוקפין אי בעו בארביסר אי בעו בחמיסר! -- the walled on whichever day they wish

answered_by.gloss_en: אמר קרא בזמניהם -- the time of this one is not the time of that one (= p_bizmaneihem)

objections.gloss_en: ואימא בתליסר! -- say the walled on the thirteenth
הכי קאמר: אלא שושן דעבדא כמאן? לא כפרזים ולא כמוקפין! -- on our tanna, Shushan follows neither class

answered_by.gloss_en: אמר רבא, ואמרי לה כדי: שאני שושן הואיל ונעשה בה נס (= p_shani_shushan_nes)

objections.gloss_en: אלא לרבי יהושע בן קרחה ... עיר ועיר למאי אתא? -- the doubled 'city' has no task on his view

answered_by.gloss_en: אמר לך רבי יהושע בן קרחה ... אלא קרא לדרשה הוא דאתא, וכדרבי יהושע בן לוי (= p_kra_lidrasha)

objections.gloss_en: ולתנא דידן מי ניחא? כיון דאית ליה פרזי פרזי, מדינה ומדינה למה לי? -- the Joshua/Ahasuerus distinction already comes from the gezera shava; unanswered, the reading is replaced by אלא קרא לדרשה הוא דאתא
ותסברא? והכתיב אלה המצות -- a prophet may not innovate anything from now on

answered_by.gloss_en: אין, מהוה הוו ... ואתו צופים ותקינו -- the forms existed; the Seers fixed which is medial and which final (= p_tzofim_kavu_mekomot)

objections.gloss_en: ועוד, האמר רב חסדא: מם וסמך שבלוחות בנס היו עומדין -- the closed forms were already in the tablets

answered_by.gloss_en: אין, מהוה הוו -- yes, both forms existed; only their placement was unknown (= p_tzofim_kavu_mekomot)

objections.gloss_en: סוף סוף אלה המצות -- even fixing their places is innovating
ותרגום של תורה אונקלוס אמרו? והא אמר רב ... מפורש זה תרגום -- the Targum existed in Ezra's day
